parties.petitioner: Fertilizers and Chemicals Travancore Ltd. & Ors.

summary: The case involved a claim for compassionate appointment by the daughter of a deceased employee who died in 1995. The employee's widow was gainfully employed at the time, making her ineligible. The daughter applied after 14 years, was initially rejected due to non-inclusion in the dependents' list, but later challenged the rejection. The High Court directed reconsideration, which was upheld on appeal. The Supreme Court examined whether a claim could be entertained after 24 years, considering that compassionate appointment is an exception to merit-based hiring under Articles 14 and 16, meant to alleviate immediate financial hardship after the death of a sole breadwinner. The Court emphasized that such appointments must comply with existing policies, have no vested right, and are not maintainable after excessive delay undermining the purpose of prompt relief.
legal_provisions_cited: Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India
Director of Treasuries in Karnataka and Anr. Vs. V. Somyashree, 2021 SCC Online SC 704
N.C. Santhosh Vs. State of Karnataka, (2020) 7 SCC 617
State of Himachal Pradesh and Anr. Vs. Shashi Kumar, (2019) 3 SCC 653
Govind Prakash Verma Vs. LIC, (2005) 10 SCC 289
Umesh Kumar Nagpal v. State of Haryana, (1994) 4 SCC 138
final_judgment: The appeal was dismissed, upholding the High Court's decision to direct reconsideration of the respondent's claim, but with the clarification that no assurance of appointment exists and that the claim must be evaluated strictly under applicable policy norms and constitutional principles.
